localChanges: chore: work towards a 3D map, not offered yet: under ?3d=1 the Riflemen, Musketmen and Marines shoulder their rifles and fire them in battle (#1360)

log: The tools models-realistic-cc0 uses to cut the Rifleman's rifle free (civ-clone/models-realistic-cc0#19): split.py, cut.py's closing, assemble.py's posed prop, stance.py's retry, normalise.py's staging matrix, and build.py's and check.py's handling of them, byte for byte the same. No model here uses them, so nothing in models/ changes; the README mentions the new keys.

The same tools/blender/rig.py and tools/check.py as models-realistic-cc0's (civ-clone/models-realistic-cc0#25), where the Riflemen, Marines and Musketmen are rigged with them: a key can hold a prop (where it points, which way its back faces, where its butt is, carried by the chest) with the hand that holds it bent to it, and grip it with the other hand; hands are laid along it at the keys and turn from key to key as the chest carries them; a prop can have a muzzle node and a back, and be left out of standing the figure on the ground; shots say what flies; keys are a frame apart; a hand out of reach fails the build; check.py refuses a joint turning over 90 degrees between frames, a prop moved where nothing holds it, and a muzzle away from its end. Nothing in this set is rigged yet, so no model changes.
The Rifleman's rifle is cut free of his back and held upright at his right side (order arms), made whole from its mirror image and rewrapped; his back, belt and hip are closed where it lay.

tools/blender/split.py (new): splits a piece fused to a figure off it by chains of stations, drops what goes with neither, closes the cut's own holes (cycles walked whichever way faces are wound, lobes, zipped, each in its own colour; original holes and two-layer sheets left), hands its staging to normalise.py, and with `mirror` gives the piece its mirror image across its middle.
cut.py: a rewrap can `close` (an OpenVDB closing), keeping every outward piece, dropping wisps, and failing where any of the piece wears away.

assemble.py: a held prop can be posed (`posed`, `top`, `ground`, `roll`); stance.py retries the bone heat without the parts held whole; normalise.py takes a staging matrix; build.py and check.py run and check all of it.
The Partisan, Warrior and Sail rebuild unchanged. Four fresh reviews; their findings are fixed, with #20, #21 and #22 left for later.

The Marine is generated again with empty hands, and holds a separately generated rifle by its grip, muzzle down. The Musketman, a community British redcoat before, is generated as a line infantryman in a plain grey coat (the owner's colour on it), holding a separately generated flintlock musket at the order. Both stand with their arms at their sides; four new generated sources (CC0, made with AI); the community redcoat's source and credit are gone. A fresh review's Medium and Lows are fixed; #24 is left.

The Riflemen, Marines and Musketmen are rigged: they keep their weapons in their hands through every clip, carry them at port arms (the Marines at the low ready) as they walk, and in a fight bring them to the shoulder in both hands, fire, hold still a moment, take the kick and bring them back. The Riflemen and Musketmen fire once at 0.54 s, the Marines a three-round burst at 0.5, 0.667 and 0.833 s; each shot is a bullet leaving from the weapon's muzzle. They die as the Partisans do, the weapon lying beside them.

tools/blender/rig.py, and check.py to match: a key can hold a prop (`hold`: where it points, which way its back faces, where its butt is, carried by the chest) with the hand that holds it bent to it, and grip it with the other hand (`grip`); each hand is laid along the prop at the keys as its forearm carries it and turns from key to key as the chest carries it, eased. A prop can have a `muzzle` node and a `back`, and be left out of standing the figure on the ground (`grounded`); shots say what flies (`kind`); keys are a frame apart; the report gives grip, wrist and elbow figures, and a hand out of reach fails the build. check.py also refuses a joint turning over 90 degrees between frames, a prop moved on the hand where nothing holds it, and a muzzle away from its end. The Partisan rebuilds unchanged.
Five fresh reviews; their findings are fixed. #26 is left (an arm bent from nearly straight moves fast for a frame as a hold starts or ends).
